gaps: P0: nothing; P3: nothing; P5: nothing better than the 1890s photochrom
notes: P1: #3 is the Leuven strip cut from the Braun and Hogenberg vol. 1 plate that also shows ’s-Hertogenbosch and Mechelen; the Rijksmuseum dates this impression 1588 (a later Kempen/Brachel printing), so the plate year 1572 is used. The vol. 3 (1581) plan (#1, #2, #4–#6) is a flat street plan. P2: Merian’s 1654 panorama (#7) is a good black-and-white alternative to de Smet; #10 is a detail of #9. #8 (Strada, 1727 edition) shows a skirmish and a hanged man in the foreground, so it would need the event flag and its plate may predate 1727. #13 is the same photochrom as #12. #17 and #18 are lions (German ‘Löwen’), not Leuven. Agence Rol’s 1914 photo of St. Peter’s (#19) shows the church before the August 1914 fire; it is a single building, and the date is that of the agency record, so it was not used. #20 is a scratched 1914 print. #21/#22 are dull rooftop views, #24 the M Leuven museum courtyard.
